assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept | The Sword low-resolution ordinary enemy sprites. Make a brand-new design and draw a matching pair of full-body gameplay key poses. Image 1 is the original tiny game sprite sheet, for creature identity and face direction only. Image 2 is the in-house pixel-art quality target for its chapter: crisp angular silhouettes, deep colored shadows, big balanced flat clusters and a few bright material edge highlights. Do not copy its creature or ornaments. Use bold and organic 16-bit forms with varied diagonals and anatomically sensible joints rather than rigid blocks and mirrored geometric pieces. Visible low-resolution square pixel grid is consistent, 1px ink outline, no blur, no gradients, no tiny dithering, no high-resolution illustration. The brightest pixels are small and belong to surface reflections, not neon eyes. Muted dark fantasy color with light-dark separation, cool or warm material accents. Low top-down with full front body visible (up to 15 degrees off forward). Light from top/front. Place ONLY two poses in this wide image, left idle, right contact; identical creature, anatomy, scale, and square pixel size. Both feet/bodies land on a common baseline, each half has plenty of margin and the gap between figures is fully empty. True transparent alpha. Do not add lettering, props, ground, effects or cast shadows.
MOB-015 waterway shell crab. Silhouette at native scale is roughly 52×32. It is a low living rock crab, not a robot. A thick arch of flaked green-grey carapace, like slabs of soaked slate with a chipped lighter lip, and a thin exposed pale seam directly above the soft underside. Two or three ivory barnacle knobs concentrated on one corner, not a tower. Small beady eyes on short stalks under the brow. Four jointed gray crab legs per side with hooked feet; allow far legs to naturally overlap where appropriate. A huge rusty crusher claw on screen-left with long irregular opposing fingers and a clear dark open gap, smaller narrow cutter claw on the right. Left pose tucks the crusher high beside the shell as a guard; body low, feet spread. Right pose pivots to the viewer and snaps that same large crusher down and toward the camera, the enlarged foreshortened pincher clearly in front of the body, other claw held back, legs braced diagonally. Show the ivory seam as the shell tilts. Make the front claws and exact same shell damage memorable; angular wet edge lights and strong deep occlusion. No grid holes or man-made metal plates, no square shell or rounded tower. Key hero silhouette is the living crab with uneven claws.

Use case: identity-preserve. Make a surgical revision of this existing The Sword shell crab two-cel design. Keep left idle exactly as shown. In the right attack pose, the large screen-left rusty claw is the same formidable angular claw coming forward at the viewer, but is caught at the instant of a SNAP with the pincer's jaws firmly CLOSED. Angle the point toward screen-left so the silhouette is quick and wide. It hovers just above the lowest toe line instead of dropping beneath it; the same planted left and right feet define the shared baseline between poses so there is no floating. Keep shell's exact chipped slate contours and barnacles, tan seam, beady eyes, tiny right claw, natural bent crab legs, restrained wet edge highlights, bold organic angular 16-bit pixel art and the same camera orientation. Both poses must have complete uncut silhouettes with space on all sides and fully clear gap, face forward. Preserve image proportions, transparent alpha, no floor line, ground, scenery, text, labels or shadow.
